# Dynamic Programming, Greedy and Amortisation

Each page contains **one mathematical formula worth memorising**, the meaning of each symbol, a substituted example, a correctness derivation, and conditions under which the formula or technique fails.

1. [DP = precise state, recurrence, base](01-dp-state-recurrence-base.qmd)
2. [Knapsack = take or skip](02-dp-knapsack-choice.qmd)
3. [LIS = smallest feasible tail for each length](03-lis-invariant.qmd)
4. [Greedy = exchange with an optimum](04-greedy-exchange-argument.qmd)
5. [Amortised proof = count total movements](05-amortised-two-pointer.qmd)
6. [Subset membership = one bit](06-bitmask-subset-recurrence.qmd)

Use these as **recall cards**, not as a bag of disconnected algorithms. Practise rebuilding the reasoning from the smallest example. Related full lessons live in the [Algorithms section](../../../../algorithms/index.qmd).
